Commentary.Commentary: All set for India's reply! The umpires are out in the middle and the 70,000-plus crowd inside the MCG eagerly awaits. The Australian players have taken their places and it will be skipper Rohit Sharma who will open the innings for India alongside Yashasvi Jaiswal. Mitchell Starc will take the new ball and he is raring to go. Let's play...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Right then, Australia have put on 474 big runs on the board and their pacers will have their tail up. The pitch and weather conditions are stellar for batting but that uneven bounce might be a huge factor and all eyes will be on Pat Cummins because he is the one who generally hits that short of a good length more often than anyone. Don't go anywhere as India's first innings is up next.

India might not have had much of a say in this Test so far but they will be mighty pleased to pick up those remaining three wickets after Lunch for just 20 runs and have managed to keep Australia under the 500-run mark. It still is a huge ask for them to get close to the Aussie total but the batting conditions at the MCG at the moment are pretty good. Also, it will be interesting to see whether Rohit Sharma does open the innings for India or does he slot into that number 3 role of Shubman Gill.

Well then, India have finally managed to clean up Australia for 474 and Jasprit Bumrah ends up with a four-fer. It was a bit of a bizarre start post Lunch as a lapse in concentration cost Mitchell Starc his wicket and then Steven Smith got out in a fashion that was obnoxious even for him. The final pairing of Nathan Lyon and Scott Boland showed some resistance but eventually, Lyon fell. However, this innings will be remembered for the fireworks up top provided by debutant Sam Konstas and then a stellar century from Steven Smith.

OUT! LBW! Another confident appeal for LBW and once again, the finger goes up! Lyon reviews it straightaway but starts to walk back to the dugout. He then waits for the decision to be made. Bumrah bowls it on a good length, and slants it into the batter. It skids through very quickly and hurries the batter into the shot. Nathan Lyon hops on the back foot and looks to work it across into the leg side but plays all over it. The ball passes very close to the bat and pings his pad. Nothing on UltraEdge. Now, interestingly, the Ball Tracking shows the ball hitting the top of the middle on the umpire's call. Luck with Bumrah as the umpire gives it out. He gets his fourth wicket. Lyon gets his marching orders and Australia are all out on a mammoth total of 474.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 2! The umpires have taken their places and so have the Indian fielders. Steven Smith is back out in the middle and has Mitchell Starc to accompany him at the crease for Australia. Spin to kick off the session as Ravindra Jadeja is all set to bowl. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, we have had just four sessions of play so far in the Boxing Day Test and it seems, Australia are throwing the punches that are dealing the most damage to the opposition and they will be eyeing up the 500-run mark before thinking about declaration. India on the other hand will be hoping that Bumrah comes out fresh post-Lunch and their pacers are able to clean up the Aussie tail at the earliest. Join us at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT) to find out how it all pans out in the afternoon session.

With the likes of Jasprit Bumrah and Akash Deep tired from their long spells early in the session and Mohammed Siraj simply not in his element, India had to resort to spin in the latter half of the session. It was Ravindra Jadeja who got rid of Cummins on 49 which seemed to have open a door for India but they failed to make the most of it yet again and are now lagging behind quite a lot already.

It was of utmost importance for Australia that Steven Smith remained at the crease heading into Day 2 and boy, didn't he roll back the years! Along with skipper Pat Cummins, Smith added 112 runs for the 7th wicket and even brought up a sensational 34th Test ton and isn't showing any signs of slowing down, in fact, he has been more aggressive since reaching triple digits.

At 299/6 and quite a flat pitch on display, India had to make use of the uneven bounce on offer with the second new ball. Jasprit Bumrah kept things tight and troubled the outside edge as well and even Akash Deep bowled a few decent deliveries every now and then but they couldn't get that breakthrough, allowing Australia to just ease into the morning session.

LUNCH, DAY 2! SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 143 runs, and 1 wicket! With how proceedings ended on Day 1 of the Boxing Day Test, everyone knew that the first session on Day 2 would be crucial. India had the second new ball and were expected to do some damage but Australia simply blew them off and are in command heading into the Lunch interval.
Spears it full in length, on off, Starc drills it straight to the covers. And that will be LUNCH ON DAY 2!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Unarguably, Australia's hour. This seventh-wicket stand between Smith and Cummins has already added 72 runs now and has proved to be the cog in the wheel for India's late surge on the first day. But in all fairness, the Indian bowlers have looked out of plans. Barring Bumrah, hardly anyone has created chances or troubled the batters. And one feels that the Indians have gone a bit more defensive, just waiting for the batters to commit a mistake. Their best bet was to run through the Aussie tail with the new ball, but they just couldn't utilize it to their benefit. As things stand, Australia are marching towards a mammoth total now and India need some really extraordinary stuff from their bowlers to get rid of Smith, who is on the cusp of a well-deserved century. Cummins too, has provided an exceptional support under pressure.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for Day 2 to begin! It is cooler compared to the first day and a bit overcast, which might help the pacers extract some movement. The umpires are in position and the Indian players have started to take their places on the field as well. The Indian players are wearing the black armbands to pay tribute to the passing of the former Indian Prime Minister, Dr. Manmohan Singh at the age of 92. The duo of Steven Smith and Pat Cummins is all set to resume their overnight stay at the crease as well. It will be Mohammed Siraj to begin proceedings with the ball here. Let's go...

While Australia's 311 puts them in a solid position, with Steve Smith holding fort on an unbeaten 68, their ambitions of a match-defining 450-plus total now hinge on his ability to marshal the tail. The morning session looms as a critical phase with the new ball that's still swinging and the odd one getting that extra bite, combined with fresh Indian bowlers hunting in the right areas, could quickly wrap up the Australian innings. Yet if Smith can weather the early storm and find support from the lower order, Australia could well dash India out of the contest. Who will dominate the proceedings on the second day? We will find out together. Stay tuned as the first ball of Day 2 is not far away from now.

One might argue that India's initial struggles stemmed from bowling a bit too short and wide of the stumps, giving Australian batters free rein. Yet a mid-day adjustment to fuller lengths and stump-focused lines finally brought the some control, significantly curbing the scoring rate, before Steven Smith and Alex Carey formed a solid partnership of 65 runs to give Australia that one more push in the final session which took them beyond the 300-run mark.

While Australia dominated most of the day on a pitch where it had a fair share of something for both batting and bowling, India found their bite in the final session courtesy of a Jasprit Bumrah special. The ace paceman redeemed himself and flipped the script with a devastating spell, that saw Australia stumble from a position of strength at 237/2 to a wobbly 246/5 in just a handful of overs. But it was Washington Sundar who provided the crucial breakthrough, prizing out a well-set Marnus Labuschagne to trigger Australia's late collapse. The off-spinner's timely strike opened the floodgates, before Bumrah capitalized with his lethal spell that transformed a day of Australian dominance into a fascinating contest heading into Day 2.

Australia may have finally cracked their opening conundrum, thanks to a dazzling debutant who fears no reputation. Sam Konstas announced himself on the Test stage with a electrifying run-a-ball fifty, bringing a breath of fresh air to Australia's top order. The newcomer's audacity was on full display as he took on India's spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, unfurling several adventurous reverse lap shots that spoke volumes of his confidence. Including him, the top 4 notched up their respective fifties and put the hosts under commanding position.

Hello, everyone! The Boxing Day Test at the illustrious Melbourne Cricket Ground continues and we are here for you with all the coverage of Day 2. The opening day was absolutely action-packed and the spectators had every single penny worth it. The match hangs pretty much in balance after what prevailed on the first day, with the momentum slightly tilted towards hosts. However, the tourists, India pulled back things to balance it out. As a result, out of three sessions played so far, both teams have won one session each, with one being a shared one.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, on the surface, it seems like Australia are in command but given the up and down we have seen on Day 1, it isn't going to be as easy to bat on going forward and India will be eyeing up early wickets on Day 2. If Australia get anywhere close to 400 runs, then India will have to bat out of their skins to even things up but that's for later. Day 2 will begin on Friday, 27 December at 5 am IST (11.30 pm GMT, the previous day) but you can join us an hour in advance for the build-up. Cheers!

The third and final session was where things came back to life and a lot happened in it as well. For the first 45 minutes or so, the pair of Marnus Labuschagne and Steven Smith dominated proceedings. All of the top 4 Aussie batters notched up half-centuries but Marnus fell right after the drinks break, triggering a mini-collapse that saw India pick up 3 wickets in the space of 9 runs. But that was as good as it got for the visitors for a while as Smith piled on the runs and Alex Carey gave him good support, playing positive strokes. However, Akash Deep dug in deep and bowled a pearler with the second new ball to Carey, allowing India to get into the Aussie tail before the day ended.

The first session belonged to Australia even after Ravindra Jadeja sent back Konstas for 60 and it was then in the second session that everything just started to slow down. Khawaja raked in a half-century as well but fell after playing a poor shot and India managed to keep the scoring rate to a minimum and got some teeth into the game.

The Boxing Day Test began with a few quiet overs from the Indian pace duo of Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj but once Usman Khawaja got that first boundary away off Siraj, the 19-year-old debutant, Sam Konstas came into life. He didn't care for Bumrah's stature or his excellence and simply took him down, even managing to hit a reverse-lap six off him, a six that Bumrah conceded after 4484 balls in Test cricket.

An engrossing and entertaining Day 1 of the Boxing Day Test, two big teams playing in front of about 87,000-plus fans at the Colosseum of world cricket that is the Melbourne Cricket Ground - it simply doesn't get better than this! At the end of the day though, it will be the Aussies who will be the happier of the two sides heading into Day 2 but not by much and will look to put a substantial first-innings score on the board.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the third and final session of the first day of this fourth Test. The umpires walk out to the middle, followed by the Indian players who spread out to the field. Marnus Labuschagne, unbeaten on 44, and Steven Smith, on 10, will resume their batting for Australia. Ravindra Jadeja (11-2-33-1) will get the proceedings underway in the third session. Off we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

It was only until Jasprit Bumrah was summoned back into the attack that India were able to break the stand. He struck gold on the very first ball of his new spell and broke the growing stand for the second wicket. Steadying gradually in his inning, Labuschagne along with Smith saw through the session. Well then, the second session has flown by on this first day. Australia holds the aces as we speak and with the batting expected to get better with the progression in the final session, India will be aiming to get some quick wickets and run through the middle order. Australia will be keen to build on this score without losing many wickets. Stay tuned as we bring all the action to you in the post-Tea session which begins at 10.02 am IST (4.32 am GMT).

Despite the testing conditions, especially from Siraj who peppered Marnus with several body blows, both batters showed admirable resilience which only furthered frustrations in the Indian camp. Their patient partnership proved valuable, with Khawaja eventually reaching his half-century and the two adding crucial 65 runs together. Though the Indian bowlers maintained a good mix of disciplined lines and lengths after Lunch, with the odd one bouncing off the pitch, and also bringing back spin in the form of Jadeja into the attack, they struggled to find that crucial breakthrough.

Coming into the second session, things did slow down a bit from the batting perspective as Bumrah and Akash Deep delivered four maidens on the trot to begin with. It was relatively slow going from Marnus Labuschagne and Usman Khawaja as they just tried to bide their time at the crease, having a good score on the board already. Conditions got a bit overcast and the ball started to nip back and nibble away off the deck for the pacers. The first hour proved particularly challenging, with just 26 runs added to the total.

TEA, DAY 1 - Session Summary - 28 overs, 64 runs, 1 wicket. Australia will be really pleased with how things have progressed for them in these first two sessions of play. But since runs came in at a sedate pace, this session will be shared by both sides. The hosts, however, find themselves in a commanding position with all batters chipping in with crucial contributions.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 1 here at the MCG! Rohit Sharma can be seen giving his players a real pep talk before taking to the field once again. The umpires are out in the middle and the Aussie pairing of Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne is all set to resume their stay at the crease. Akash Deep to begin proceedings with the ball, let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, with the mercury levels about to reach 40 degrees Celsius or so in the afternoon session, we might see it all boil up in the next session. When these two teams are involved, it surely won't be a quiet one for sure. A mighty crucial session on Day 1 awaits, so, do join us around 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

India did get their teeth into the contest after the second drinks break and the bowling changes did turn out to be successful. Akash Deep kept things tight and it was Ravindra Jadeja who got them the vital breakthrough but overall, they weren't able to induce many opportunities. Australia have 112 runs on the board with Usman Khawaja set and Marnus Labuschagne looking comfortable too and they will be looking to consolidate after the break.

Australia got the opportunity to bat first but those first few overs showed that they were a bit nervy and young Sam Konstas played one too many shots. However, they were lucky not to edge deliveries and were beaten past the bat which allowed Konstas to just keep going at it and once he got a couple of balls away, runs just started to pour. Konstas took down Bumrah for 14 runs in one over and then 18 in another as he brought up a sensational half-century before falling on 60.

India were asked to bowl first on a warm morning in Melbourne but there was an even covering of grass to aid the pacers and it certainly did in the first couple of overs as Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj both began with maidens. Soon enough though, they were put to the sword and a few heated exchanges between Siraj and Konstas and even one in particular where Virat Kohli gave Konstas a slight shrug of the shoulder, all only added to India's misery. Bumrah even conceded a six in Test cricket after 4000 plus deliveries.

The iconic 'Boxing Day Test' at the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground and two of the toughest competitors going head-to-head, what more can one even ask for? Well, that first session was just a complete embodiment of the occasion as debutant Sam Konstas lit up the arena in front of about 90,000 fans before finally falling and now that the dust has settled, the post-Lunch session should be very intriguing.

Bumrah wraps up the session by bowling it on a good length, sliding down leg. Marnus Labuschagne misses to glance it away. Pant behind the wickets moves to his left and collects it. And that will be LUNCH ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Well, a nerve-jangling and action-packed first 45 minutes for sure. Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj initiated the attack from the Indian side asking all the right questions initially and beating the edges on multiple occasions. However, as per the on-air commentators, the pacers were a tad bit short in their lengths. The two Aussie openers negotiated the first thirty minutes with alert. Konstas then, true to his anticipators, threw caution to the wind and announced himself with some really audacious shots on his debut against one of the best bowlers in the world. Runs have come at a brisk pace after that with the bowlers finding next to little help from the surface from those lengths. India would be desperate enough to get their first breakthrough and the hosts would aim to see through this session going unscathed. Let's see how the next phase of play pans out. Commentary.Commentary: What an electric atmosphere out there! We are done with 'Jan Gan Man' and 'Advance Australia Fair', and it is now time for the action to begin at the iconic 'G'. It is a full house and the two umpires are greeted with the sun shining to its glory. Rohit Sharma leads the Indian team to the middle as they walk out to spread out to their respective fielding positions. Out come the two Australian openers. It is the new pair of Usman Khawaja and the debutant Sam Konstas who walk up to the crease. As usual, Jasprit Bumrah will kick off the proceedings with the new ball for India. Three slips and a gully for him in readiness. And we are off and running...

We are just a few moments away from this Boxing Day Test to get underway. But, before that, the two stalwarts of the game, Adam Gilchrist and Irfan Pathan walk out with the shining trophy and carefully place it on the podium. A special mention about match referee Andy Pycroft, who will be officiating in his 100th Test match. Now, the two sets of teams stride out and line up for their respective national anthems followed by the match officials. It will be India's first, followed by Australia's national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Mark Nicholas and Sunil Gavaskar are inspecting the Day 1 pitch at Melbourne. Mark starts and says that it is pretty hot out there. Adds that heavy roller is doing its job and also states that there's a lot of grass on the surface. Adds it is a fresh pitch and there will be plenty in it for the pacers. Gavaskar then says that the grass will die down and it will get better for the batters as the game progresses. Mentions that it is slightly tacky and the first two hours will be a bit tough for the opening batters. Mark concludes by saying that 92,000 tickets have been sold and they can't wait for the games to begin.

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Rohit Sharma (C), Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant (WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar (In for Shubman Gill), Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep.

Australia (Playing XI) - Usman Khawaja, Sam Konstas (In for Nathan McSweeney), Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Pat Cummins (C), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Scott Boland (In for Josh Hazlewood).

Rohit Sharma, the captain of India, says they would have batted as well. Mentions it looks a good pitch and they will have to bowl well. Adds that there's a lot to play for and this gives another opportunity to play good cricket with whatever the situation lies in front of you. Says it is a new day and it is all about fighting and showing good character. Informs they have made one change, Shubman Gill misses out and Washington Sundar comes in for him. Also informs that he will bat at the top of the order.

Pat Cummins, the captain of Australia says that they will have a bat first. Reckons that the surface looks good and has some grass on it as well. Adds that it's been a great series so far and there's great anticipation for this game. Informs that Sam Konstas is making his debut and Scott Boland also comes in for Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in the favor of Australia and Pat Cummins elects to BAT first.

The mighty MCG, standing tall and proud, expects close to 90,000-odd staunch cricket fans to fill its stands. As things stand, if Australia dominates and wins, they'll keep their hopes alive and have a shot at claiming the trophy in the final Test. However, India simply needs to avoid defeat at the MCG to retain the trophy. Even if India loses the final Test after securing win at the MCG, they'll keep the Border-Gavaskar Trophy since a drawn series means the current holder retains the trophy. The atmosphere is electric and festive, charged with anticipation as both India and Australia know that victory here could be the decisive step toward the World Test Championship final. The stakes couldn't be higher, and the stage couldn't be grander. A lot is at stake here with crucial WTC points up for grabs. Let’s find out together who dominates. Toss and teams coming up very shortly.

Following the grand retirement of the crafty offie Ravichandran Ashwin, India has brought in the promising young spinner, Tanush Kotian, though his spot remains uncertain with experienced Washington Sundar also in contention. The pressure will again fall on Jasprit Bumrah, who leads the charge with 21 wickets, the most in the series. Akash Deep and Mohammed Siraj complete a pace attack that’s been impressive as well.

India's batting troubles persist, with KL Rahul being their sole pillar of consistency. Others have blown hot and cold, failing to string together solid performances. Captain Rohit Sharma's form is particularly worrying, his quiet bat and unsettled batting position causing headaches before the Boxing Day Test. Virat Kohli has a century to his name this series but needs to deliver more, though his love affair with the iconic 'G', where he holds the team's best batting average, offers hope. Lower down, young gun Nitish Reddy and the battle-hardened Ravindra Jadeja have shown impressive grit and character.

The Australian middle order packs a serious punch, with Steven Smith and Marnus Labuschagne gradually finding their groove. But it's Travis Head who's been the real 'Head-ache' for India this series, topping the run-scoring charts with his trademark swashbuckling style. While a quad strain in Brisbane had the Aussie camp holding their breath, Head's been deemed fit to participate. Alex Carey has been equally dependable, shepherding the lower middle order with vital contributions. Meanwhile, the two pace stalwarts Mitchell Starc and skipper Pat Cummins will be aiming to replicate their form this time around as well.

Australia's momentum in this series has been somewhat dampened by their opening woes. The musical chairs at the top of the order after Warner’s retirement continues to spin, with the latest chapter seeing Nathan McSweeney shown the exit after a string of below-par performances. Enter Sam Konstas, a wonderkid who's been turning heads in domestic cricket with his consistent run-scoring. Fresh off a ton against Prime Minister’s XI, the young gun now finds himself thrust into the pressure cooker of a Boxing Day Test, tasked with solving Australia's opening puzzle with Khawaja. Also, in the bowling department, Scott Boland, who, in fact looked equally threatening in Adelaide Test, replaces injured Josh Hazlewood.

After a gripping series thus far, both teams have traded punches and we find ourselves at this pivotal moment. India's commanding victory in the series opener in Perth was answered magnificently by Australia's resilience and domination in the second in Adelaide, followed by a draw at the Gabba, which, was marred mostly by rain, but in all fairness, it threw a lot of entertainment and tense moments as well with the momentum swinging back and forth.

Hello, everyone! The hallowed turf of the Melbourne Cricket Ground awakens on this crisp morning after Christmas, as cricket's most storied rivalry prepares to write its next chapter. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy of 2024/25, delicately poised at 1-1, resumes its thrilling narrative on Boxing Day, a date that holds near-religious significance in the cricketing calendar.
